When we look inside models, we see that they don't just represent the next word.

They often plan many words into the future, and work backwards from their plan to decide on the next word.

This is part of what lets them to do complex tasks despite outputting one word at a time!

Looking inside models can help resolve some apparent contradictions!

For example, how come models can solve hard math problems and write coherent essays if they're only predicting one word at a time?

Humans need to plan ahead to do these tasks.

It turns out, models do as well!

We see parts of the model that specialize in representing a plethora of concepts. Simple colors, nuanced emotions, etc.

What's more, models use these parts to better predict what comes next.

To predict what a character in a play will say, models learn to infer their emotions!

This should be familiar to us!

When speaking, I say one word at a time, but I'm thinking of a broader point I'm making, and of where it leads.

We see the same patterns in LLMs. They output one word at a time, but represent a broader goal and can plan many words ahead.

🧠 What makes a good explanation in mechanistic interpretability?

Easy-to-understand examples aren't enough. Neither is high feature activation.

Our ICML 2026 Spotlight asks how explanations can be both interpretable to humans and faithful to the model. https://t.co/CI3hDDncYZ

Many Mech Interp methods rely on top-activating samples (Top-K) to explain features.

Mathematically, this amounts to hard selection, which can bias explanations toward extreme-activation patterns.

Our view replaces hard selection with KL-minimal soft reweighting (KLSC). https://t.co/whFBeOd0pb

What does this look like in practice?

On DINOv3 SAE features, EnergyDPS generates clear and strongly activating evidence.

Compared with Top-K retrieval, MACO, and DiffExplainer, our samples reveal more recognizable visual patterns.

Here are two examples: ❤️ 🪽 https://t.co/DKpSJZhygk

Across 100 DINOv3 SAE features, EnergyDPS achieved the highest interpretability ratings from human, GPT, and Gemini evaluators in our blinded study.

The bigger message: explanations should be understandable and grounded in model responses. https://t.co/nvQaqtVqCx
